ic_name: SD Memory Card (SD Simplified Physical Layer Specification)
initialization_sequence: 1. Power-up: Host ramps VDD from 0 V to operating range (2.7-3.6 V) within VDD ramp-up time.
2. Host waits ≥ 1 ms after VDD reaches operating range, then drives ≥ 74 dummy CLK cycles with CMD held HIGH so the card can stabilize its internal clock.
3. Host issues CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE, no response) → card enters Idle state, RCA = 0x0000.

4. Host issues CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND) with VHS = 0001b (2.7-3.6 V) and a check pattern (e.g. 0xAA). v2.0+ card returns R7 echoing the pattern; v1.x card returns no response → host marks the card as v1.x.
5. Host enters ACMD41 loop: CMD55 + ACMD41 with VDD window + HCS=1 (host supports SDHC) + S18R=1 (host requests 1.8 V) until OCR bit 31 (BUSY) reports 1. Loop timeout = 1 second.
6. Read OCR.CCS (bit 30) — 0 = SDSC, 1 = SDHC/SDXC. Read OCR.S18A — 1 = card accepts 1.8 V.
7. (Optional UHS-I) If S18A=1, host issues CMD11 (VOLTAGE_SWITCH); card pulls CMD/DAT LOW; host stops CLK, switches VDDIO to 1.8 V, restarts CLK; card releases CMD/DAT HIGH within ≤ 1 ms.
8. Host issues CMD2 (ALL_SEND_CID) → card publishes 128-bit CID in R2 → card enters Identification state.
9. Host issues CMD3 (SEND_RELATIVE_ADDR) → card publishes new 16-bit RCA in R6 → card enters Stand-by state.
10. Host issues CMD9 (SEND_CSD with RCA) → R2 with 128-bit CSD; host extracts capacity, CCC, TRAN_SPEED.
11. Host issues CMD7 (SELECT_CARD with RCA) → R1b → card enters Transfer state.
12. Host issues CMD55 + ACMD51 (SEND_SCR) → SCR returned on DAT0 → host learns supported bus widths and spec version.
14. (Optional) Host issues CMD6 (SWITCH_FUNC, Mode 1, Function Group 1 = High Speed) → card returns 512-bit status on DAT; if accepted, host can now drive CLK at up to 50 MHz.
15. (Optional UHS-I) Host issues CMD19 (SEND_TUNING_BLOCK) repeatedly while sweeping the sampling phase to find the optimal window (CMD19 mandatory for SDR104).
16. (SDSC only) Host may issue CMD16 (SET_BLOCKLEN) to choose a block length other than 512. SDHC/SDXC ignore CMD16 for read; block length is fixed at 512.
17. Card is now ready for data transfer commands (CMD17/CMD18/CMD24/CMD25).
single_block_read_sequence: 1. Host issues CMD17 (READ_SINGLE_BLOCK) with the byte (SDSC) or block (SDHC/SDXC) address.
2. Card returns R1; card enters Sending-data state.
3. Card drives Start bit (LOW) on each active DAT line, then 512 bytes (4096 bits) of payload, then 16-bit CRC16 per active DAT line, then End bit (HIGH).
4. Host verifies CRC16; if mismatch, host may re-issue CMD17 to retry.
multi_block_read_sequence: 1. (Optional) Host issues CMD23 (SET_BLOCK_COUNT) with the number of blocks.
2. Host issues CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) with start address.
3. Card returns R1 and streams consecutive blocks on DAT lines, each with Start bit + 512 B + CRC16 + End bit.
4. If CMD23 was used, transfer ends after the pre-defined count. Otherwise host issues CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION) to terminate.
single_block_write_sequence: 1. Host issues CMD24 (WRITE_BLOCK) with the byte (SDSC) or block (SDHC/SDXC) address.
2. Card returns R1; card enters Receive-data state.
3. Host drives Start bit (LOW) on each active DAT line, then 512 B payload, then 16-bit CRC16 per DAT line, then End bit (HIGH).
4. Card returns Data Response Token on DAT0: 010 = accept, 101 = CRC error, 110 = write error.
5. Card pulls DAT0 LOW (busy) while programming the block to flash. Card enters Programming state.
6. When programming complete, card releases DAT0 HIGH and returns to Transfer state.
7. Host may poll CMD13 (SEND_STATUS) on the CMD line during Programming.
multi_block_write_sequence: 1. (Optional) Host issues CMD55 + ACMD23 (SET_WR_BLK_ERASE_COUNT) to pre-erase the target range for speed.
2. (Optional) Host issues CMD23 (SET_BLOCK_COUNT) with the number of blocks.
4. Card returns R1; host streams consecutive blocks with Start/CRC16/End framing.
5. Host issues CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION) if CMD23 was not used.
6. Card programs the buffered blocks; DAT0 LOW until complete.
7. Host may issue CMD55 + ACMD22 (SEND_NUM_WR_BLOCKS) to read back the number of successfully written blocks.
erase_sequence: 1. Host issues CMD32 (ERASE_WR_BLK_START) with start block address.
2. Host issues CMD33 (ERASE_WR_BLK_END) with end block address.
3. Host issues CMD38 (ERASE) with the desired operation in the argument (Erase / Discard / FULE).
4. Card returns R1b and pulls DAT0 LOW during the erase.
5. When complete, card returns to Transfer state.
voltage_switch_sequence_uhs_i: 1. Host completes CMD0 / CMD8 / ACMD41 with S18R=1 and confirms OCR.S18A=1.
3. Card returns R1 with current state = Ready.
4. Within Nrc CLK cycles after R1 end-bit, card drives CMD and DAT0..DAT3 LOW to indicate voltage-switch handshake.
5. Host stops CLK for at least 5 ms, switches VDDIO from 3.3 V to 1.8 V.
6. Host restarts CLK at the new voltage.
7. Within 1 ms, card releases CMD and DAT0..DAT3 HIGH. Bus is now at 1.8 V signaling and host may proceed with UHS-I modes (SDR12/SDR25/SDR50/DDR50/SDR104).
tuning_sequence_uhs_i_sdr104: 1. Host enters SDR104 mode (after CMD6 switch and CMD11 voltage switch).
3. Card returns the 64-byte tuning pattern on DAT lines.
4. Host compares received pattern to expected; adjusts sampling phase.
5. Repeat across the sampling-phase range to find the largest pass window; pick window center.
hot_removal_recovery: 1. Host detects card-detect transition (mechanical switch or CD/DAT3 pull-up sense).
2. Host aborts any pending command, flushes its own buffers, and resets the host controller.
3. On next insertion, repeat the full initialization sequence from step 1 of initialization_sequence.
